title: Hausdorff's Free Subgroup of SO(3), as an Honest Subgroup
description: Upgrades the parent's Hausdorff theorem (the rotation group of ℝ³ contains a free group of rank 2, proved through the underlying linear equivalences ≃ₗ) into a statement internal to the isometry group ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³ (the orthogonal group O(3); the two generators are rotations, hence lie in SO(3)). Packages the result the way group theory wants it: a forgetful monoid hom (ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ ℝ³) →* (ℝ³ ≃ₗ ℝ³), an injective FreeGroup Bool →* (ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ ℝ³), a subgroup S with FreeGroup Bool ≃* S (a literal copy of F₂ inside SO(3)), and a concrete pair of non-commuting rotations. Fully verified, 0 axioms, 0 sorries — none of the results depend on the parent's banach_tarski axiom.

meta.author: Hausdorff, F. (1914), formalized in Lean 4 with Mathlib

Bundles a multiplicative map between groups into a MonoidHom (map_one is derived) — builds toLinearEquivHom from just multiplicativity

An injective group hom f gives G ≃* f.range — turns the free embedding into a literal copy FreeGroup Bool ≃* S of F₂ inside the isometry group

overview.historicalContext: Felix Hausdorff's 1914 *Grundzüge der Mengenlehre* contained the algebraic discovery that powers the Banach–Tarski paradox: the rotation group SO(3) contains a free subgroup of rank 2. Two rotations by arccos(1/3) about perpendicular axes generate a free group — no nontrivial reduced word in them is the identity — proved by an algebraic-number-theoretic argument (a nontrivial word applied to a test vector produces coordinates in ℤ[√2] whose residues mod 3 can never return to the start). This single fact, that F₂ embeds in SO(3), is what makes the sphere paradoxical: the paradoxical self-decomposition of the free group is transported, via the embedding, to a paradoxical decomposition of S². Tarski's 1938 theorem then frames the conceptual chain F₂ ↪ SO(3) ⟹ SO(3) non-amenable ⟹ B³ paradoxical. The parent gallery entry (lebesgue-measure-oq-06) proves Hausdorff's theorem, but records freeness through the *underlying linear equivalences*, forgetting that the generators are isometries. This entry restores that information and packages the embedding as group theory uses it — an injective homomorphism and an honest isomorphic subgroup — so the phrase 'SO(3) contains a copy of F₂' becomes a literal Lean statement.
overview.problemStatement:
**Open Question (lebesgue-measure-oq-06-oq-01)**: Formalize Hausdorff's free subgroup theorem in SO(3) — i.e. realise the rank-2 free embedding internally to the three-dimensional rotation/isometry group, and package it as an injective homomorphism and an isomorphic subgroup.

**Result**: toLinearEquivHom (the forgetful monoid hom O(3) →* GL bridging the two settings); hausdorff_free_subgroup_isometry (FreeGroup.lift into ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³ is injective); isometryGroup_contains_freeGroup (an injective FreeGroup Bool →* O(3)); exists_freeGroup_mulEquiv_rotationSubgroup (a subgroup S with FreeGroup Bool ≃* S); and exists_noncommuting_rotations (a concrete non-abelian witness).
overview.text: The rotation group of ℝ³ contains a free group of rank 2 — stated inside the isometry group ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³ rather than through its underlying linear equivalences — and therefore contains a literal isomorphic copy of F₂ and a pair of non-commuting rotations.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Proof Strategy.**

1. `toLinearEquivHom`: build the monoid hom (ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³) →* (ℝ³ ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³), e ↦ e.toLinearEquiv. Multiplicativity is exactly `LinearIsometryEquiv.toLinearEquiv_trans`: both groups compose on the underlying maps (a * b = b.trans a), so `MonoidHom.mk'` needs only `map_mul` and derives `map_one`.
2. `hausdorff_free_subgroup_isometry`: extract φ, ψ from the parent's `hausdorff_free_subgroup`. The parent's lift into linear equivalences factors as `toLinearEquivHom ∘ (our lift into isometries)` — proved by `FreeGroup.ext_hom`, since both monoid homs agree on the two generators. Injectivity of the parent lift then forces injectivity of ours: if `lift g x = lift g y` apply `toLinearEquivHom` to both sides.
3. `isometryGroup_contains_freeGroup`: `FreeGroup.lift (b ↦ if b then φ else ψ)` *is* a homomorphism FreeGroup Bool →* O(3), and step 2 gives its injectivity.
4. `exists_freeGroup_mulEquiv_rotationSubgroup`: feed that injective hom to `MonoidHom.ofInjective`, yielding FreeGroup Bool ≃* f.range — a subgroup of the isometry group isomorphic to F₂.
5. `freeGroup_of_true_false_ne`: the generators a, b of FreeGroup Bool satisfy a·b ≠ b·a — map into S₃ = Perm (Fin 3) sending them to the transpositions (0 1), (1 2), whose products differ by `decide`.
6. `exists_noncommuting_rotations`: if φψ = ψφ then the injective hom would force a·b = b·a in F₂, contradicting step 5.
keyInsights: **Freeness is forgetful-stable.** A linear *isometry* is in particular a linear *equivalence*, and that forgetful map is an injective group homomorphism. Injectivity of a homomorphism out of F₂ is detected after any further homomorphism, so freeness proved in the ≃ₗ world is automatically freeness in the ≃ₗᵢ world — no orbit argument is reproved.

**The composition convention is the whole content of the bridge.** `M ≃ₗᵢ[R] M` and `M ≃ₗ[R] M` both define a * b = b.trans a; matching those conventions is exactly what makes e ↦ e.toLinearEquiv multiplicative (`LinearIsometryEquiv.toLinearEquiv_trans`), so `MonoidHom.mk'` suffices.

**'Contains a copy of F₂' is `MonoidHom.ofInjective`.** An injective hom is the same data as an isomorphism onto its range; that is the precise Lean meaning of SO(3) ⊇ F₂, and it is the structural fact the Banach–Tarski paradox actually consumes.

**Non-abelianness for free.** Two distinct free generators never commute, and this transfers along any injective hom — so the abstract freeness immediately yields concrete non-commuting rotations, the geometric obstruction that SO(2) (abelian) lacks.

The group structures on M ≃ₗ[R] M and M ≃ₗᵢ[R] M and the forgetful map between them
MonoidHom.ofInjective (an injective hom is an isomorphism onto its range)

sections.summary: Imports the parent LebesgueMeasureOQ06 (for hausdorff_free_subgroup), states the goal — upgrading Hausdorff's theorem into the isometry group and packaging it as an honest subgroup — and introduces the abbreviations Rot3 = ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³ (the rotation/isometry group O(3)) and Lin3 = ℝ³ ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³.

sections.title: The Forgetful Bridge O(3) →* GL
sections.summary: toLinearEquivHom: the monoid homomorphism (ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³) →* (ℝ³ ≃ₗ[ℝ] ℝ³), e ↦ e.toLinearEquiv, built with MonoidHom.mk' from multiplicativity (LinearIsometryEquiv.toLinearEquiv_trans + LinearEquiv.mul_eq_trans). toLinearEquivHom_apply records the defining equation.
sections.mathContext: A linear isometry is a linear equivalence: the forgetful map is a group homomorphism $O(3) \to \mathrm{GL}(\mathbb{R}^3)$.

sections.title: Hausdorff's Theorem, Internal to O(3)
sections.summary: hausdorff_free_subgroup_isometry: the parent's lift into linear equivalences factors through toLinearEquivHom (proved by FreeGroup.ext_hom), so injectivity transfers to the lift into the isometry group. isometryGroup_contains_freeGroup repackages it as an injective FreeGroup Bool →* ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³.
sections.mathContext: $\langle \varphi, \psi \rangle \le O(3)$ is free of rank 2: $\mathrm{FreeGroup}\,\mathrm{Bool} \hookrightarrow O(3)$.

sections.title: A Literal Copy of F₂ in SO(3)
sections.summary: exists_freeGroup_mulEquiv_rotationSubgroup: applying MonoidHom.ofInjective to the free embedding gives a subgroup S of the isometry group together with a group isomorphism FreeGroup Bool ≃* S.
sections.mathContext: $\exists\, S \le O(3),\ \mathrm{FreeGroup}\,\mathrm{Bool} \cong S$ — $SO(3)$ contains a copy of $F_2$.

sections.title: Non-Commuting Rotations
sections.summary: freeGroup_of_true_false_ne: the two generators of FreeGroup Bool do not commute (via a decidable map to S₃ = Perm (Fin 3)). exists_noncommuting_rotations: transports this along the injective hom to produce two rotations φ, ψ with φψ ≠ ψφ — a concrete non-abelian witness for SO(3).

crossReferences.description: The parent proves Hausdorff's free subgroup theorem with injectivity stated for the underlying linear equivalences; this entry lifts it into the isometry group O(3) and packages it as an injective homomorphism, an isomorphic subgroup FreeGroup Bool ≃* S, and non-commuting rotations

conclusion.summary: Complete, fully verified (0 sorries, 0 axioms) realisation of Hausdorff's free subgroup of SO(3) internal to the isometry group: a forgetful bridge O(3) →* GL, the injective free embedding FreeGroup Bool →* (ℝ³ ≃ₗᵢ[ℝ] ℝ³), the isomorphic subgroup FreeGroup Bool ≃* S, and explicit non-commuting rotations. None of the results depend on the parent's banach_tarski axiom.
conclusion.implications: Turns the parent's existence statement into the structural fact the Banach–Tarski paradox consumes: SO(3) contains a literal copy of the rank-2 free group F₂. The forgetful-stability argument (freeness in ≃ₗ ⟹ freeness in ≃ₗᵢ) is reusable for any representation that factors through a faithful homomorphism, and the non-abelian witness marks exactly where the 2-dimensional case (SO(2) abelian, amenable) fails to produce a paradox.
openQuestions: Show the generators have determinant +1, placing the free subgroup in SO(3) (special orthogonal) rather than merely O(3) at the Lean level.
Derive non-amenability of the isometry group directly: any group containing F₂ is non-amenable, closing the chain to the parent's free_group_not_amenable.
Transport the free group's paradoxical decomposition along the embedding to a paradoxical decomposition of S² minus a countable set (the full Hausdorff paradox).
